cause: On May 27, 2013, protests broke out in Istanbul over government plans to turn Taksim Gezi Park, one of the last remaining green spaces in the city, into a shopping center. These protests quickly escalated into widespread anti-government unrest, fueled in part by the violent police response to peaceful demonstrations. On June 1, Facebook, Twitter, and 3G mobile networks were reportedly throttled to unusable speeds. Throttling gives governments plausible deniability of censorship, since slow loading times can be blamed on network congestion, especially during mass protests where many people are gathered in a small area. However, users reported VPNs restored access to social platforms, and over 120,000 people in Türkiye installed HotSpot Shield.
